topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Framing of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and framing cancer development as an adaptive evolutionary process influenced by mutations, cell types, and the microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution and Epigenetic Drivers of Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how tumors evolve through sequential genetic mutations, competitive clonal selection, and non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tissue Hierarchy, Stemness, and the Cell of Origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how normal tissue stem cell hierarchies and cell-of-origin characteristics influence cancer initiation and tumor-propagating potential across leukemias and solid tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Promotion of Tumor Growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how permissive microenvironments, chronic inflammation, and supportive stroma act as essential non-mutational promoters for tumor outgrowth and provide targets for therapy.

topics.label: Methods for Investigating Tumor Evolution and Spatial Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the genomic sequencing, computational modeling, and spatial profiling technologies used to study tumor heterogeneity and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Summary of Multi-Factorial Cancer Evolution and Concluding Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the lecture's core themes regarding the co-evolution of mutations, cell lineage, and environmental factors, concluding the session.
